summary: Transport an intentionally closed Blender transmissive solid through glTF volume, transmission and IOR extensions into a Three.js physical material while preserving thickness units and attenuation meaning.
objective: A closed test fixture with baked or explicitly declared thickness variation becomes progressively more attenuated at larger thickness values, keeps a stable thin-wall fallback, and exposes unsupported runtime refraction instead of silently presenting alpha-blended glass.
intent_signals: thick glass has no depth color after export
attenuation distance changes with model scale
example_prompts: Carry this thick colored-glass bottle from Blender into Three.js with visible path-length attenuation.
Diagnose why my closed transmissive solid still renders like an infinitely thin sheet.
not_for: Open surfaces, cutout foliage or gauze whose transparency is coverage.
Participating-media scattering, dispersion or nested-volume certification.

principles: Volume is an extension contract layered on transmission: nonzero thickness changes a thin surface into a boundary around a homogeneous medium, so the authoring mesh must close that medium.

Keep scale explicit. glTF thickness is expressed in mesh coordinate space and follows node transforms, while attenuation distance is expressed in world-space units; an accidental scale change alters the apparent absorption path.
Base color tints the boundary response; attenuation color and distance describe color change along travel through the medium. Do not tune them as interchangeable color pickers.
IOR controls dielectric reflection and volume refraction through its extension. It is a material input, not proof that the runtime resolves every overlapping or nested refractive surface.
This record transports parameters and states observable consequences. General optics and artistic glass-lighting choices remain in the linked material and lighting profiles.
implementation: In Blender, use a closed, consistently oriented mesh for the volumetric region. Connect transmission and supported volume absorption through the glTF exporter arrangements; record Blender version, export extensions and object scale.

Choose thicknessFactor in mesh-coordinate units and, when thickness varies, supply a Non-Color thickness texture in its specified green channel. Keep a simple constant-thickness wedge beside the production mesh for diagnosis.

Export KHR_materials_transmission with KHR_materials_volume and KHR_materials_ior when nondefault IOR is intended. Inspect extensionsUsed and the actual material JSON rather than assuming the viewport node graph was transported.

After GLTFLoader, inspect the MeshPhysicalMaterial transmission, thickness/thicknessMap, attenuationColor, attenuationDistance and ior values. Record Three.js revision and renderer/backend; test support on every claimed target.
Provide an explicit fallback state: thin transmissive surface, opaque stylized shell or disabled feature notice. Do not silently substitute low-opacity blending for an unsupported thick-volume claim.
observable_checks: A fixture using a baked thicknessMap or separate stepped materials with explicit thickness values shows stronger attenuation at larger declared thickness while equal-thickness regions remain consistent under fixed lighting; geometry alone is not treated as proof of the raster thickness estimate.

Uniformly scaling the asset and its declared world relationship produces the expected documented change or is compensated by an explicitly revised attenuation distance; no hidden unit conversion occurs.
Setting thickness to zero selects the declared thin-wall comparison and removes the path-length-dependent volume effect without changing alpha coverage.

The loaded material inventory and glTF JSON show transmission and volume extensions and values. KHR_materials_ior is present when a nondefault IOR is intended; when omitted, the inspection records the extension default of 1.5. Unsupported backends are recorded as unavailable rather than passed.

creative_affordances: Exaggerate attenuation color or thickness zoning for a stylized prop when the result is identified as authored appearance.
Choose a thin-shell or opaque cutaway fallback when runtime volume support would obscure the object or exceed the interaction budget.
known_limits: KHR_materials_volume specifies a homogeneous absorbing medium and excludes scattering; the thickness texture is a lossy real-time approximation.
Nested transparent layers, scene-object refraction and backend support remain renderer-specific and require runtime inspection.
No material constants are claimed as measured values, and no Blender export or Three.js render was run for this record.

claims.statement: The ratified KHR_materials_volume extension requires a transmissive extension to take effect, defines nonzero thickness as a volume boundary around a homogeneous medium on a closed manifold mesh, stores thickness texture values in green multiplied by thicknessFactor, expresses thickness in mesh coordinate space and attenuationDistance in world space, and excludes scattering.
claims.scope: KHR_materials_volume extension contract for homogeneous absorbing media; implementation notes do not guarantee a specific raster refraction algorithm.

claims.scope: Ratified glTF extension parameters and current Three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial API; actual GLTFLoader mapping and renderer/backend output require version-specific runtime verification.
